title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens identify noncanonical translation factor eIF2A as an enhancer of SARS-CoV-2 programmed -1 ribosomal frameshifting
model: HEK293T with a SARS-CoV-2 -1 PRF dual-fluorescence reporter, genome-wide GeCKOv2 knockout library (123,411 guides, 1,000 non-targeting controls)
contrast: GFP/mCherry-low vs -high (reduced frameshifting) FACS sort, day 14 and day 7, paired across 2 replicates (2 vs 2)
paper_calls: day 14: 5 enriched + 4 depleted genes at FDR 0.10 (EIF2A top enriched); day 7: 4 enriched + 12 depleted (EIF2A #15)
barcs_calls: day 14: 35 genes at FDR 0.10 (15 against the control null, controls well-calibrated at p05 0.048); day 7: 43 genes (13 against the control null)
named_hits: EIF2A recovered as the top enhancer at day 14 (BARCS enriched rank 1, FDR 3.7e-11) and at day 7 (enriched rank 6, FDR 0.018)
verdict: BARCS confirms the paper's headline hit EIF2A as the strongest frameshift enhancer at day 14 and recovers the paper's suppressor set (GET4/BAG6/DNAJC24), with a well-calibrated non-targeting control null; it calls a somewhat longer list than the paper's sparse RRA hits.
